title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 229 (Penalty for furnishing false statement, mutilation, destruction of documents)

content.overview: Section 229 provides that where a person is required to answer any question put to him or furnish any information or produce any book or paper under this Chapter, and he makes a statement which is false in any material particular knowing it to be false, or suppresses any material fact, or mutilates, destroys, falsifies or secretes any book or paper, he shall be liable to the punishment provided in the section. The provision is the investigation-specific false-statement and document-interference offence. Related general false-statement and fraud provisions under the Act (including sections 447 and 448) may also apply on appropriate facts.
content.glance: False statement knowing it to be false, or suppression of material fact, or mutilation/destruction/falsification/secretion of books in connection with Chapter XIV examination or production → punishable under s. 229; distinct from general fraud (s. 447) and false statement (s. 448) routes.
content.study: Where a person who is required to answer any question put to him or furnish any information or produce any book or paper in the course of inspection, inquiry or investigation under this Chapter makes a statement which is false in any material particular knowing it to be false, or omits any material fact knowing it to be material, or mutilates, destroys, falsifies or secretes or is privy to the mutilation, destruction, falsification or secretion of any book or paper, he shall be punishable with the imprisonment and fine the section provides. Current-law framing: identify the duty to answer, furnish or produce under the Chapter; establish false statement with knowledge, or suppression of material fact with knowledge, or interference with books; apply the section’s penalty. Cross-refer ss. 447 and 448 where the facts also engage general fraud or false-statement offences.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Person required under Chapter XIV to answer a question, furnish information, or produce a book or paper.

sections.heading: Conduct
sections.body: Makes a statement false in a material particular knowing it to be false; or suppresses a material fact knowing it to be material; or mutilates, destroys, falsifies or secretes (or is privy to such acts regarding) any book or paper.

sections.heading: Penalty
sections.body: Punishable as the section provides (imprisonment and fine as stated in the Act).

sections.heading: Related Offences
sections.body: General false-statement (s. 448) and fraud (s. 447) provisions may also apply on appropriate facts; s. 229 is the Chapter XIV-specific route.

provisions.title: Penalty for furnishing false statement, mutilation, destruction of documents

examples.title: False answer to inspector
examples.body: During a s. 217 examination a director knowingly states that no related-party transfers occurred when large transfers are documented. Section 229 applies to the false statement made under the Chapter.

examples.title: Destruction of books
examples.body: An officer destroys statutory registers after notice of investigation. Section 229 covers mutilation, destruction, falsification or secretion of books in connection with the investigation process.

hypotheticals.question: Is an innocent mistake in an answer to an inspector automatically an offence under s. 229?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 229 targets a statement that is false in a material particular knowing it to be false, or suppression of a material fact knowing it to be material, or intentional interference with books. An honest mistake without knowledge of falsity is not the same as the knowing false-statement ingredient.

distinctions.title: False statement in investigation (s. 229) vs general false statement (s. 448)
distinctions.left: False statement, suppression or document interference in the course of Chapter XIV inspection/inquiry/investigation
distinctions.right: General false statement in any return, report, certificate, financial statement or other document under the Act

misconceptions.trap: Any incomplete answer to an inspector is automatically fraud under s. 447.
misconceptions.correction: Section 229 is the Chapter XIV-specific false-statement and document-interference offence with its own ingredients (including knowledge of falsity). Section 447 fraud has separate ingredients. Both may apply on appropriate facts, but they are not automatic substitutes.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 229 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm duty under Chapter XIV. II. Test false statement with knowledge / suppression / document interference. III. Apply penalty. IV. Note ss. 447/448 if relevant. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Duty facts; falsity and knowledge; document acts; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 229 punishes a person required under Chapter XIV to answer, furnish information or produce books who knowingly makes a materially false statement, suppresses a material fact, or mutilates, destroys, falsifies or secretes books or papers.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Integrity of the investigation process is protected by specific criminal liability for knowing falsehood and interference with documentary evidence.
